why: Implementing four stacks requires a consistent shared-array partition scheme across initialization, push and pop, with distinct empty and full bounds for every stack, including the last partition. This is a complete adaptation of a stack implementation with several coupled index invariants, rather than one supplied push/pop operation. Fixed partitions suffice; dynamic space sharing is not required, so Hard is not justified.

The question assesses a concrete C record containing another record and field input/output. It does not assess an abstract data type or its interface. A specific subtopic is preferable because none of the listed fundamentals subtopics describes nested records accurately; the rubric allows an unlisted subtopic where needed.

Defining Student with a nested Date and reading/displaying fields assesses C record composition, not ADT abstraction or interface design. Use the same specific fundamentals subtopic as the equivalent employee-record question.

Correct undo/redo code must coordinate two histories, transfer operations or states in the right direction, and invalidate redo history after a new edit. Naming stacks does not supply this application logic. The rubric rates combining familiar structures or adapting a known algorithm Medium; these obligations go beyond isolated push/pop snippets.

The required output converts null links into predecessor/successor threads on a given BST. No traversal procedure or traversal sequence is requested. Construction is the assessed operation; use a specific subtopic rather than mislabeling it Threaded tree traversal. Its hand-simulation difficulty remains Easy.

This program combines FIFO registration/service with deletion by arbitrary patient ID. It must keep both directions and the queue endpoints consistent for interior, head, tail, singleton and empty-list cases. The rubric assigns standard algorithms with several interacting cases Medium. Retain the existing caveat that the supplied struct omits prev; do not silently assume the contradictory representation is resolved.

The question asks when explicit-stack iteration or recursive execution is preferable. It asks neither for a base case nor for call tracing. Keep Recursion as the topic, but use a subtopic that reflects the requested comparison; Easy remains appropriate.

The required program maintains a priority-ordered container across insertion and removal, rather than merely tracing dequeue order. Correct ordered insertion and highest-priority removal must agree on ordering and endpoint/empty cases. This fits a standard implementation with several invariants; no heap or optimal complexity requirement supports Hard.

Implementing search through threads requires defining link/tag semantics and correctly choosing between a successor thread and descent to the leftmost node of a real right subtree, including termination. These representation-dependent cases distinguish it from a basic recursive traversal. A prebuilt tree removes thread construction, but does not remove the multi-case traversal implementation.

The student must translate scheduling requirements into priority-aware C operations and choose a representation and service policy. That is a design/adaptation task under the rubric, not a supplied priority trace or isolated queue operation. The old reason uses the two-mark allocation to support Easy, which the rubric explicitly disallows. Do not assume a particular aging or fairness algorithm absent from the prompt; the priority-based design alone supports Medium.

Maximum Depth of Binary Tree computes a root-to-leaf height, whereas this question requires the longest leaf-to-leaf path, combining two branches and handling nodes without two leaf-bearing subtrees. Height is only a helper computation, so #104 omits the decisive algorithmic step. The catalog contains no diameter problem; return [] rather than recommend a broad tree-recursion prerequisite.
